stem: A 56-year-old man comes to the office due to several months of progressive neck swelling.  He has also had intermittent epistaxis and headaches.  The patient has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medications.  He does not use tobacco or alcohol.  Twelve years ago, he emigrated from rural China to the United States.  Physical examination shows several enlarged, firm, and nontender cervical lymph nodes.  Nasopharyngeal evaluation reveals a mass arising from the pharyngeal recess.  Histopathologic examination of the mass shows undifferentiated malignant cells of epithelial origin.  Further analysis of these cells is most likely to reveal the presence of nucleic acid sequences from which of the following viruses?​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​​
explanation:
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is an epithelial tumor that arises in the pharyngeal recess and classically presents with a neck mass, nasal obstruction, and a unilateral middle ear effusion.  It can also cause epistaxis and headaches.  Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is endemic to southern China, where genetic and dietary factors (eg, consumption of salted fish) promote premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial lesions.  Subsequent malignant transformation is then induced by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

EBV is a ubiquitous human herpes virus that causes infectious mononucleosis in a minority of patients (primary infection is usually asymptomatic).  Initial infection is followed by lifelong latent infection in memory B cells.  While latent, the EBV genome exists as an episome in the nucleus of infected cells and expresses a subset of EBV genes (latency genes) which do the following:

  • Promote periodic viral reactivation from memory B cells, leading to recurrent (asymptomatic) mucosal infections

  • Induce genetic instability by inhibiting DNA repair

  • Inhibit apoptosis to promote survival of infected cells

  • Allow evasion of the immune system by impairing antigen presentation and inducing T-cell anergy

Together, these effects can lead to malignant transformation of infected B cells (eg, Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma) or premalignant epithelial cells (eg, nasopharyngeal carcinoma).

(Choices A and C)  Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) are both herpes viruses; as such, they cause acute infection followed by latent disease.  Although CMV can reactivate in immunocompromised patients (eg, HIV, posttransplantation) and cause severe end-organ diseases (eg, retinitis, gastroenteritis), it is not an oncogenic virus.  HHV-8 reactivation also occurs primarily in immunocompromised individuals and is associated with Kaposi sarcoma.

(Choice D)  Patients living with HIV have an increased risk for cancer, mostly due to immunosuppression that increases susceptibility to oncogenic viruses and increases immune system evasion by malignant cells.  HIV has much less of a direct carcinogenic impact.

(Choice E)  Human T-cell lymphoma leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) infects T cells and can lead to acute adult T-cell leukemia lymphoma and HTLV-1–associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis; it is not associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

Educational objective:Nasopharyngeal cancer is endemic to southern China due to genetic and dietary factors that promote premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial lesions.  Subsequent malignant transformation occurs due to the infection of premalignant cells with Epstein-Barr virus.​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​​
